summary: At zero-based segment 0 step 47, the wizard has selected ordinary throne effect 7. C begins the court-summoning loop; JavaScript calls courtmon() but records note_unported('makemon.c makemon') instead of creating the selected monster. C therefore consumes the monster-placement and creation calls, produces a monster, and updates the screen, while JavaScript skips all of those effects. The queue labels C's next RNG entry collect_coords(teleport.c:700), a downstream placement helper; the source defect is the skipped makemon call in sit.c:throne_sit_effect.

source.branch: C sit.c:throne_sit_effect() case 7 sets cnt=rnd(10), emits the throne voice, then repeats (void)makemon(courtmon(), tx, ty, NO_MM_FLAGS) while cnt--. This is an ordinary throne effect, after the wizard selected effect 7; the chosen throne is not a special Vlad's Tower throne.
callers: C sit.c:dosit() calls throne_sit_effect() for an ordinary throne. JavaScript js/sit.js:dosit reaches throne_sit_effect() through the same sitting command path.
C mkroom.c:courtmon() selects and returns each court monster type. JavaScript js/mkroom.js:courtmon() already implements this selector and preserves its two source RNG calls.

C makemon.c:makemon() receives the selected type at the hero's coordinates with NO_MM_FLAGS and relocates that request through enexto_core(). JavaScript js/makemon_create.js:makemon_runtime() wraps the existing makemon() implementation and supports this explicit-species, explicit-coordinate, no-flags runtime shape.
dependencies: The current JavaScript branch already has the matching courtmon() result and the makemon_runtime() helper is already implemented for explicit-species creation at the hero square with NO_MM_FLAGS. The missing behavior is the caller invocation in throne_sit_effect; no collect_coords or courtmon implementation change is indicated by this trace.
